content.text:
Best match is Li8ZrO6 (mp-755225) plus Li3Mn4O8 (mp-1291742). I read peak positions by counting points along the grid, so they're good to about ±0.1–0.3°. Confidence is moderate, not high.

- **Li8ZrO6 (mp-755225):** Its strong simulated peaks near 17.0, 19.3 and 21.7° match observed peaks at 16.9, 19.2 and 21.6°. Further observed peaks at about 29.3, 34.0, 36.5, 37.7 and 39.0° fit the rest of its pattern from a hand calculation of the cell. Observed positions sit slightly low, as expected from strain.
- **The unexplained 18.4° peak:** The strongest observed peak (100) is at 18.4°, and Li8ZrO6 has nothing there.
- **Li3Mn4O8 (mp-1291742):** Its simulation has one dominant peak near 18.4–18.5° and only weak ones elsewhere, so it adds little that would conflict with the pattern. I didn't check its other peaks against the data one by one.
- **Rejected:**
  - KReO4 needs a strong peak near 26–27° that isn't there.
  - Y5(ReO6)2 needs a strong peak at about 12.3° that isn't there.
  - Zn2Co3O8 has several further strong peaks that don't show up in the observed pattern.
  - The perovskites (Sr2TaVO6, Eu2ZnWO6, SrNiO3, LaRuO3) don't fit the low-angle peaks. I judged this from their cells and didn't simulate them.

Two things don't fit cleanly. The observed 36.5° peak is stronger than Li8ZrO6 alone predicts, possibly because a Li3Mn4O8 peak overlaps it. A peak near 41.0° also isn't clearly explained by either phase.
